items.title: British meteorologists: 20th century climate is gone
items.summary: The hottest day of the year is now 4.5 degrees hotter than just a few decades ago in south-east England, states the British Met Office. "These data show that the climate of the 20th century is now gone".
items.summary_original: Årets varmaste dag är numera 4,5 grader hetare än för bara några decennier sedan i sydöstra England, konstaterar brittiska Met Office. ”Dessa data visar att 1900-talets klimat nu är borta”.

items.title: Attacked girl has been allowed to leave the hospital
items.summary: The five-year-old girl who was attacked and seriously injured in a playground in Helsingborg no longer needs medical care, the Public Prosecutor's Office states in a press release.
items.title_original: Attackerad flicka har fått lämna sjukhuset
items.summary_original: Den femåriga flickan som attackerades och skadades allvarligt i en lekpark i Helsingborg behöver inte längre sjukvård, uppger Åklagarmyndigheten i ett pressmeddelande.

items.title: Government puts pressure on EU ahead of Commission’s review of EU Emissions Trading System
items.summary: Next week, the European Commission will present its review of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). Sweden’s Minister for EU Affairs Jessica Rosencrantz has sent a letter to the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union, with Sweden’s priorities and standpoints ahead of the upcoming negotiations.

items.title: EU adopts sanctions over poisoning of Russian opposition politician Alexei Navalny
items.summary: In light of the poisoning of Alexei Navalny, the EU has adopted sanctions against six Russian individuals under the chemical weapons sanctions regime. In June, listings of seven individuals and one entity were also adopted under the EU Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime, which was established because of the internal oppression in Russia.

items.title: Government invests SEK 250 million in global health
items.summary: The Government has adopted a new support package for global health, including sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), totalling SEK 250 million for 2026. The health package consolidates Sweden’s commitment to improving the health of the most vulnerable through vaccines in low- and middle-income countries and increased access to maternal and newborn care where the needs are greatest.

items.title: The ESRB warns of vulnerabilities in the financial system linked to advanced AI models
items.summary: The European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB), the EU's macro-supervisory body, issues a formal warning about vulnerabilities in the financial system linked to advanced AI models. The ESRB's warning calls on relevant authorities to take such risks into account in supervision and monitoring.
items.title_original: ESRB varnar för sårbarheter i det finansiella systemet kopplade till avancerade AI-modeller
items.summary_original: Europeiska systemrisknämnden (ESRB), EU:s makrotillsynsorgan, utfärdar en formell varning om sårbarheter i det finansiella systemet, kopplade till avancerade AI-modeller. ESRB:s varning uppmanar relevanta myndigheter att ta hänsyn till sådana risker i tillsyn och övervakning.

items.title: NATO selects Saab GlobalEye Airborne Warning and Control System
items.summary: Today, 7 July, in connection with the NATO Summit in Ankara, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte announced that NATO has chosen Saab’s GlobalEye as its new Airborne Early Warning & Control (AEW&C). This means that NATO will open negotiations with Saab to purchase up to 10 GlobalEye aircraft.

items.title: From Kiev to Kyjiv – Sweden changes Embassy name
items.summary: On 2 July 2026, Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard announced that the Swedish names of the Embassy of Sweden in Kyiv and the Honorary Consulate of Sweden in Odesa will be changed to reflect the Ukrainian names for Kyiv and Odesa, respectively.

items.title: Poland procures three A26 submarines from Saab following talks with Swedish Government
items.summary: On 29 June, Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson visited Gdynia, Poland for government-level talks. The meeting focused on strengthened bilateral cooperation between Sweden and Poland in the areas of regional security and defence. Minister for Defence Pål Jonson, Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard, Minister for Culture Parisa Liljestrand, Minister for Infrastructure and Housing Andreas Carlson and Minister for EU Affairs Jessica Rosencrantz also took part on the trip.

items.title: Sweden provides SEK 25 million to earthquake-stricken Venezuela
items.summary: The two earthquakes in Venezuela on 24 June have had a profound impact on the Venezuelan people and exacerbated an already difficult humanitarian situation. Sweden is now providing SEK 25 million in humanitarian assistance to Venezuela to support initiatives such as the distribution of food packages, access to clean water, temporary emergency shelter, protection of vulnerable groups and reunification of children and families who have been separated.

items.title: Government overhauls development assistance to Africa, Latin America and Asia
items.summary: The Government has adopted nine new development assistance strategies which will provide a total of around SEK 6 billion for development cooperation in Africa, Latin America and Asia. The new development assistance will be based on evidence of what works and produces concrete results.
